My decision rested on Apple's just-reported fiscal 2024 results (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024): Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year total net sales of $391.0 billion with net income of $93.7 billion, or $6.08 per diluted share — figures I cross-checked against Apple's own newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. I deliberately discarded one search result (stock-highlights.net) that listed fiscal 2024 net sales as "$391.0 million" and net income as "$93.7 million," since that's inconsistent with both primary sources by a factor of 1,000. Note that the $6.08 EPS includes a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge, so underlying earnings power is somewhat stronger than the headline; combined with the stock sitting near $222 on steady sentiment around iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, I judged the risk/reward attractive enough to establish a starter position (about 20% of available cash). I did not exceed the per-order cap, and there is remaining capacity of roughly $10,188 under today's $20,000 limit should you want a second tranche; the main risks I'd watch are Greater China demand and a slower-than-hoped Apple Intelligence feature ramp.
